LESSON: COMPUTER CONCEPTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Foundations of Pre- Technical studies
Topic 1.3: Computer Concepts
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Computer Concepts, part of Foundations of Pre- Technical studies in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: when using the digital device for learners with visual difficulties. 1. Why are there different classes of computers? 2. How are computers classified?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Computer Concepts together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
●Critical thinking and problem solving: interpretation and inference skills are developed as the learner matches different types

of computers to their respective classes.

●Communication and collaboration: teamwork skills are developed as the learner discusses the types of computers in a user

environment.

Values:
Peace: the learner displays tolerance when discussing the classification of computers.

PCIs:

Safety and security: Cyber security is enhanced as the learner accesses internet and downloads and watches a video clip on the

classification of computers.

8

Link to other subjects:

Mathematics as the learner uses a calculator.
